Newsletter

Inside Creative Mentoring.

Creative Mentoring is designed as an ongoing conversation around your work, not as a sequence of generic exercises. Each week, you submit work in progress, finished pieces, questions or visual research through your private Padlet. I review what you send and respond with focused written feedback that looks at the decisions behind the work: composition, visual hierarchy, rhythm, materials, narrative, intention and the relationship between technique and meaning.

The aim is not simply to correct individual images. We use each submission to understand how your visual language is developing and to decide what deserves attention next. Depending on your needs, I may propose a new exercise, a reference, a technical adjustment, a compositional alternative or a short audiovisual explanation created specifically for your process.

This allows the mentorship to remain flexible while still keeping a clear rhythm. Your work determines the direction, and the feedback helps you turn intuition into more conscious decisions. Over time, Padlet becomes a visual record of your evolution, where you can see recurring ideas, changes, discoveries and the connections between one week and the next.

The goal is to help you build a more coherent, personal and independent way of working, so that the decisions you make during the mentorship continue to support your practice after it ends. The final review brings these threads together and identifies useful directions for continuing your work independently. The process is personal: two artists may receive very different exercises or resources because the mentorship responds to the questions, strengths and obstacles visible in each individual body of work.
